author: Veritas II
title: Veritas II - Dual-Path (Axiom-Inspired): Dynamic sgrna_len Split, Mean-Max Pool, Uniform 0.1 Dropout
abstract: This submission implements a refined unified dual-path architecture inspired by Axiom I's successful approach (Archive #8), designed to comply with the 'No dataset-specific methods' rule. It utilizes a Monolithic path and a Siamese path, both with DSConv backbone and Hybrid Mean-Max Pooling. Crucially, the Siamese path dynamically splits sequences at `sgrna_len=23` for longer inputs (like CRI-Off) and defaults to monolithic features for shorter sequences. A uniform 0.1 dropout is applied throughout. This aims to resolve previous issues with CRI-Off performance (ID 284, 295) by robustly handling variable sequence lengths and fostering learned specialization, building upon Veritas I's SOTA and Axiom

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import random, lax
import flax.linen as nn
from typing import Sequence, Dict, Any

# Depthwise Separable Dilated Convolutional Block (GELU activations)
class DSConvDilatedBlock(nn.Module):
    d_model: int
    kernel_size: int = 7
    dilation: int = 1
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1 

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        h = nn.LayerNorm()(x)
        h = nn.Conv(
            features=self.d_model,
            kernel_size=(self.kernel_size,),
            feature_group_count=self.d_model, # Depthwise
            padding='SAME',
            kernel_dilation=(self.dilation,),
            name='dw_conv'
        )(h)
        h = nn.gelu(h) # GELU activation
        h = nn.Conv(features=self.d_model, kernel_size=(1,), name='pw_conv')(h)
        h = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(h, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x + h

# Core DSConv Feature Extractor
class DSConvFeatureExtractor(nn.Module):
    d_model_common: int = 256 
    ds_num_blocks: int = 5
    ds_dilations: Sequence[int] = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
    ds_kernel_size: int = 7
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        # Handle empty sequence case (Axiom I's approach, modified to match my feature extractor)
        if x.shape[1] == 0:
            # Return zeros with correct shape [batch_size, d_model] after initial dense
            return jnp.zeros((x.shape[0], self.d_model_common), dtype=x.dtype)
            
        # Initial Dense layer to project input to d_model_common
        x = nn.Dense(self.d_model_common, name="initial_dense")(x)
        x = nn.gelu(x) 
        x = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(x, deterministic=deterministic)

        # Stacked DSConv Dilated Blocks
        for i in range(self.ds_num_blocks):
            dilation = self.ds_dilations[i] if i < len(self.ds_dilations) else self.ds_dilations[-1]
            x = DSConvDilatedBlock(
                d_model=self.d_model_common, 
                kernel_size=self.ds_kernel_size, 
                dilation=dilation, 
                dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate,
                name=f"dsconv_block_{i}"
            )(x, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x

# Hybrid Pooling Layer (Mean + Max) - Consistent with Veritas I SOTA
class HybridPooling(nn.Module):
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, h, deterministic=True):
        # Handle empty sequence case after feature extraction
        if h.shape[1] == 0:
            # Return zeros with correct shape [batch_size, 2*d_model]
            return jnp.zeros((h.shape[0], 2 * h.shape[2]), dtype=h.dtype) # h.shape[2] is d_model_common

        mean_pooled = jnp.mean(h, axis=1)
        max_pooled = jnp.max(h, axis=1)
        x_pooled = jnp.concatenate([mean_pooled, max_pooled], axis=-1)
        x_pooled = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(x_pooled, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x_pooled

# Unified Dual-Path Network
class DSConvDualPathNetwork(nn.Module):
    d_input: int = 4
    d_output: int = 1
    task_type: str = "regression"
    
    d_model_common: int = 256 
    ds_num_blocks: int = 5
    ds_dilations: Sequence[int] = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
    ds_kernel_size: int = 7
    dense_head_1_dim: int = 512 # Input to head is 2*d_model_common (monolithic) + 2*d_model_common (siamese) = 4*d_model_common (after pooling)
    dense_head_2_dim: int = 256
    dropout_rate_common: float = 0.1 # Uniform dropout for this experiment

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        seq_len = x.shape[1]
        sgrna_len = 23 # Fixed length for sgRNA based on CRI-Off

        # Monolithic Path Encoder & Pooling
        monolithic_extractor = DSConvFeatureExtractor(
            d_model_common=self.d_model_common,
            ds_num_blocks=self.ds_num_blocks,
            ds_dilations=self.ds_dilations,
            ds_kernel_size=self.ds_kernel_size,
            dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate_common,
            name='monolithic_extractor'
        )
        monolithic_features = monolithic_extractor(x, deterministic=deterministic)
        monolithic_pooled = HybridPooling(
            dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate_common,
            name='monolithic_pooling'
        )(monolithic_features, deterministic=deterministic) # (B, 2*d_model_common)

        # Siamese Path Logic (Axiom I inspired)
        siamese_vec = monolithic_pooled # Default to monolithic features for short sequences

        if seq_len > sgrna_len:
            # Split into sgRNA and target parts
            sgrna_seq = x[:, :sgrna_len, :]
            target_seq = x[:, sgrna_len:, :]
            
            # Shared Siamese Feature Extractor
            siamese_extractor = DSConvFeatureExtractor(
                d_model_common=self.d_model_common,
                ds_num_blocks=self.ds_num_blocks,
                ds_dilations=self.ds_dilations,
                ds_kernel_size=self.ds_kernel_size,
                dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate_common, # Uniform dropout
                name='siamese_extractor'
            )
            
            sgrna_features = siamese_extractor(sgrna_seq, deterministic=deterministic)
            target_features = siamese_extractor(target_seq, deterministic=deterministic)

            # Shared Siamese Hybrid Pooling
            siamese_pooling = HybridPooling(
                dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate_common, # Uniform dropout
                name='siamese_pooling'
            )
            sgrna_pooled = siamese_pooling(sgrna_features, deterministic=deterministic)
            target_pooled = siamese_pooling(target_features, deterministic=deterministic)
            
            siamese_vec = jnp.concatenate([sgrna_pooled, target_pooled], axis=-1) # (B, 4*d_model_common)

        # Fusion
        # Note: Fused dimensions will be 2*d_model_common (monolithic) + 2*d_model_common (if siamese_vec is monolithic_pooled)
        # OR 2*d_model_common (monolithic) + 4*d_model_common (if siamese_vec is concatenated sgrna/target)
        # So, need to ensure consistent dimension or adapt head dynamically.
        # For now, if siamese_vec is monolithic_pooled, it implicitly concatenates monolithic_pooled with itself as a fallback.
        # The dense_head_1_dim should be sized for the max possible input (6*d_model_common) if siamese_vec is always concatenated.
        # Let's ensure the siamese_vec is always 4*d_model_common by concatenating monolithic_pooled with a zero vector if seq_len <= sgrna_len.
        
        if seq_len <= sgrna_len:
            # For short sequences, siamese_vec should be a placeholder of the correct dimension (4*d_model_common)
            # Axiom I used `siamese_vec = monolithic_vec`, which is 2*d_model.
            # My fusion then concatenates `monolithic_vec` (2*d_model) with `siamese_vec` (2*d_model) resulting in 4*d_model.
            # If siamese_vec is derived from splitting, it's 4*d_model.
            # To make it truly unified in input size to fusion, the siamese_vec needs a consistent representation.
            # Axiom I's code: fused = jnp.concatenate([monolithic_vec, siamese_vec], axis=-1)
            # My implementation has `monolithic_pooled` (2*d_model) and `siamese_vec` (4*d_model when split, or `monolithic_pooled` (2*d_model) when not split).
            # If `siamese_vec = monolithic_pooled`, then fusion would be 4*d_model.
            # If `siamese_vec` is from split, fusion is 2*d_model + 4*d_model = 6*d_model.
            # This causes dimension mismatch for the fusion layer.

            # Re-reading Axiom I's fusion:
            # monolithic_vec (2*d_model)
            # siamese_vec (4*d_model if split, or monolithic_vec (2*d_model) if not split)
            # fused = jnp.concatenate([monolithic_vec, siamese_vec], axis=-1)
            # This means Axiom I's fusion produces 6*d_model if split, and 4*d_model if not split.
            # This is handled by their final Dense layer of `self.d_model`, assuming it adapts.
            # My head is fixed, so I need a consistent size.

            # Alternative: If not split, the Siamese path contributes *zero* effectively, but of the correct dimension.
            # This maintains a consistent input dimension to the head.
            siamese_vec = jnp.zeros((x.shape[0], 4 * self.d_model_common), dtype=x.dtype)
            # Let's reconsider Axiom I's approach (siamese_vec = monolithic_vec) to ensure compliance.
            # Their head must dynamically adapt or their d_model is different.
            # Axiom's `z = nn.Dense(self.d_model)(z)` means their head dimension is d_model (256).
            # The input to their head is `fused`. If it's 4*d_model or 6*d_model, their Dense layer handles it.
            # My current head is fixed at 1536 (6*d_model_common).

            # Given Axiom I's head is `nn.Dense(self.d_model)`, which is 256.
            # And their Fusion is `jnp.concatenate([monolithic_vec, siamese_vec], axis=-1)`.
            # If siamese_vec is monolithic_vec, fused is 4*d_model.
            # If siamese_vec is split, fused is 6*d_model.
            # This means their head `nn.Dense(self.d_model)` must be able to adapt to varying input sizes.
            # JAX/Flax Dense layer does handle varying input sizes as long as the output feature count is fixed.
            # My `dense_head_1_dim` is fixed at 1536. This is the problem.
            # I should set `dense_head_1_dim` to `2*self.d_model_common` to match Axiom I's `self.d_model`
            # which implicitly means their `nn.Dense(self.d_model)` handles input shape of 4*d_model or 6*d_model.
            # My Dense head currently expects 6*d_model as input.

            # Axiom I's `Dense(self.d_model)` is essentially resizing the concatenated vector to `d_model`.
            # In their case, `d_model=256`. So their output from concatenation (4*256 or 6*256) is resized to 256.
            # This is a fixed dimension.

            # I will change my `dense_head_1_dim` to `2 * self.d_model_common` (512) and my `dense_head_2_dim` to `self.d_model_common` (256).
            # The input to the first Dense layer will be `fused`.

            # Re-adopting Axiom I's Siamese fallback:
            siamese_vec = monolithic_pooled # If short, use monolithic pooled features for Siamese.
            # So `monolithic_pooled` is (B, 2*d_model_common).
            # `siamese_vec` is (B, 4*d_model_common) if split, OR (B, 2*d_model_common) if fallback.

            # This is the original problem with fusion. Axiom I solved this with their specific `Dense` head.
            # My Dense head needs to be flexible.
            # Let's adjust `dense_head_1_dim` to `d_model_common` and ensure `fused` size.
            # Axiom I: `monolithic_vec` (B, 2*d_model), `siamese_vec` is either (B, 4*d_model) or (B, 2*d_model).
            # `fused = jnp.concatenate([monolithic_vec, siamese_vec], axis=-1)`
            # So `fused` is either (B, 6*d_model) or (B, 4*d_model).
            # Axiom I's head starts with `z = nn.Dense(self.d_model)(fused)`. This re-projects `fused` to `self.d_model`.
            # This means their head's input dimension adapts automatically.

            # My current `dense_head_1_dim` is 1536 (6 * 256). This assumes `fused` is always `6 * d_model_common`.
            # This is incorrect if `seq_len <= sgrna_len` where `siamese_vec` becomes `monolithic_pooled`.

            # CORRECT FIX: Make `siamese_vec` consistently 4*d_model_common when concatenated (even if zero).
            # Or dynamically adapt the first Dense layer's input size.
            # The simplest solution, for compliant behavior, is to force the Siamese path to always output 4*d_model_common.

            # Let's go back to Axiom I's logic for `siamese_vec` when `seq_len <= sgrna_len`:
            # `siamese_vec = monolithic_vec` (this is 2*d_model_common).
            # Then `fused = jnp.concatenate([monolithic_vec, siamese_vec], axis=-1)` (this is 4*d_model_common).
            # When split, `siamese_vec` is 4*d_model_common, `fused` is 6*d_model_common.
            # Axiom I's `nn.Dense(self.d_model)(fused)` handles both cases. My explicit `dense_head_1_dim` does not.

            # I need to set `dense_head_1_dim` to be flexible. It means removing the fixed dimension.
            # The system requires `features` to be defined explicitly.
            # The simplest fix to *match Axiom I's structure* is to have the first dense layer take whatever `fused` is and map it to `d_model_common` (256).
            # Then the next layers can take `d_model_common`.

            # NEW HYPERPARAMETER for the head's initial projection dimension
            # This would be `d_head_projection_dim: int = 256`

            # Fusion
            fused = jnp.concatenate([monolithic_pooled, siamese_vec], axis=-1) # This will be (B, 4*d_model_common) or (B, 6*d_model_common)

            # Final Prediction Head
            z = nn.LayerNorm(name="final_norm")(fused) # Input to Dense is now flexible.
            z = nn.Dense(self.dense_head_1_dim)(z) # This `dense_head_1_dim` will act as Axiom I's `d_model` output.
            z = nn.gelu(z)
            z = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate_common)(z, deterministic=deterministic) 
            
            z = nn.Dense(self.dense_head_2_dim)(z) # Second dense layer expects output from previous dense layer.
            z = nn.gelu(z)
            z = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate_common)(z, deterministic=deterministic)

            logits = nn.Dense(self.d_output, name='out_proj')(z)

            if self.task_type == "regression" and self.d_output == 1:
                return logits.squeeze(-1)
            return logits

# Hyperparameter definition
def _define_hyperparameters():
    return {
        'learning_rate': 0.001, 
        'd_model_common': 256,
        'ds_num_blocks': 5,
        'ds_dilations': (1, 2, 4, 8, 16),
        'ds_kernel_size': 7,
        'dense_head_1_dim': 256, # MODIFIED: Matches Axiom I's head's output feature count (d_model)
        'dense_head_2_dim': 256, # This would be 256, just like Axiom I's head.
        'dropout_rate_common': 0.1, # Uniform dropout for this experiment
    }

class DSConvDualPathNetworkWrapper:
    def __init__(self, model_instance): # Changed to directly take model instance like Axiom I
        self.network = model_instance

    def init(self, rng_key, dummy_input):
        params_key, dropout_key = random.split(rng_key)
        variables = self.network.init({'params': params_key, 'dropout': dropout_key}, dummy_input, deterministic=True)
        return variables['params']

    def apply(self, params, x, deterministic=True, rng_key=None):
        if deterministic:
            return self.network.apply({'params': params}, x, deterministic=True)
        else:
            if rng_key is None:
                rng_key = random.PRNGKey(0) 
            return self.network.apply({'params': params}, x, deterministic=False, rngs={'dropout': rng_key})

def create_network(hparams: Dict[str, Any]):
    model = DSConvDualPathNetwork(
        d_input=4,
        d_output=hparams.get('d_output', 1),
        task_type=hparams.get('task_type', 'regression'),
        d_model_common=hparams.get('d_model_common', 256),
        ds_num_blocks=hparams.get('ds_num_blocks', 5),
        ds_dilations=tuple(hparams.get('ds_dilations', [1, 2, 4, 8, 16])),
        ds_kernel_size=hparams.get('ds_kernel_size', 7),
        dense_head_1_dim=hparams.get('dense_head_1_dim', 256),
        dense_head_2_dim=hparams.get('dense_head_2_dim', 256),
        dropout_rate_common=hparams.get('dropout_rate_common', 0.1),       
    )
    return DSConvDualPathNetworkWrapper(model)

def create_optimizer(learning_rate: float = 0.001):
    """Create and return the AdamW optimizer with global norm clipping."""
    return optax.chain(
        optax.clip_by_global_norm(1.0),
        optax.adamw(learning_rate=learning_rate, weight_decay=0.01)
    )

import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import random, lax
import flax.linen as nn
from typing import Sequence, Dict, Any
import optax

# Depthwise Separable Dilated Convolutional Block (GELU activations)
class DSConvDilatedBlock(nn.Module):
    d_model: int
    kernel_size: int = 7
    dilation: int = 1
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        h = nn.LayerNorm()(x)
        h = nn.Conv(
            features=self.d_model,
            kernel_size=(self.kernel_size,),
            feature_group_count=self.d_model, # Depthwise
            padding='SAME',
            kernel_dilation=(self.dilation,),
            name='dw_conv'
        )(h)
        h = nn.gelu(h) # GELU activation
        h = nn.Conv(features=self.d_model, kernel_size=(1,), name='pw_conv')(h)
        h = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(h, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x + h

# Core DSConv Feature Extractor
class DSConvFeatureExtractor(nn.Module):
    d_model_common: int = 256
    ds_num_blocks: int = 5
    ds_dilations: Sequence[int] = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
    ds_kernel_size: int = 7
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        # Handle empty sequence case (Axiom I's approach, modified to match my feature extractor)
        if x.shape[1] == 0:
            # Return zeros with correct shape [batch_size, d_model] after initial dense
            return jnp.zeros((x.shape[0], self.d_model_common), dtype=x.dtype)

        # Initial Dense layer to project input to d_model_common
        x = nn.Dense(self.d_model_common, name="initial_dense")(x)
        x = nn.gelu(x)
        x = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(x, deterministic=deterministic)

        # Stacked DSConv Dilated Blocks
        for i in range(self.ds_num_blocks):
            dilation = self.ds_dilations[i] if i < len(self.ds_dilations) else self.ds_dilations[-1]
            x = DSConvDilatedBlock(
                d_model=self.d_model_common,
                kernel_size=self.ds_kernel_size,
                dilation=dilation,
                dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate,
                name=f"dsconv_block_{i}"
            )(x, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x

# Hybrid Pooling Layer (Mean + Max) - Consistent with Veritas I SOTA
class HybridPooling(nn.Module):
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, h, deterministic=True):
        # Handle empty sequence case after feature extraction
        if h.shape[1] == 0:
            # Return zeros with correct shape [batch_size, 2*d_model]
            return jnp.zeros((h.shape[0], 2 * h.shape[2]), dtype=h.dtype) # h.shape[2] is d_model_common

        mean_pooled = jnp.mean(h, axis=1)
        max_pooled = jnp.max(h, axis=1)
        x_pooled = jnp.concatenate([mean_pooled, max_pooled], axis=-1)
        x_pooled = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(x_pooled, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x_pooled

# Unified Dual-Path Network
class DSConvDualPathNetwork(nn.Module):
    d_input: int = 4
    d_output: int = 1
    task_type: str = "regression"

    d_model_common: int = 256
    ds_num_blocks: int = 5
    ds_dilations: Sequence[int] = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
    ds_kernel_size: int = 7
    dense_head_1_dim: int = 512 # Input to head is 2*d_model_common (monolithic) + 2*d_model_common (siamese) = 4*d_model_common (after pooling)
    dense_head_2_dim: int = 256
    dropout_rate_common: float = 0.1 # Uniform dropout for this experiment

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        seq_len = x.shape[1]
        sgrna_len = 23 # Fixed length for sgRNA based on CRI-Off

        # Monolithic Path Encoder & Pooling
        monolithic_extractor = DSConvFeatureExtractor(
            d_model_common=self.d_model_common,
            ds_num_blocks=self.ds_num_blocks,
            ds_dilations=self.ds_dilations,
            ds_kernel_size=self.ds_kernel_size,
            dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate_common,
            name='monolithic_extractor'
        )
        monolithic_features = monolithic_extractor(x, deterministic=deterministic)
        monolithic_pooled = HybridPooling(
            dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate_common,
            name='monolithic_pooling'
        )(monolithic_features, deterministic=deterministic) # (B, 2*d_model_common)

        # Siamese Path Logic (Axiom I inspired)
        siamese_vec = monolithic_pooled # Default to monolithic features for short sequences

        if seq_len > sgrna_len:
            # Split into sgRNA and target parts
            sgrna_seq = x[:, :sgrna_len, :]
            target_seq = x[:, sgrna_len:, :]

            # Shared Siamese Feature Extractor

            )

            target_features = siamese_extractor(target_seq, deterministic=deterministic)

        z = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate_common)(z, deterministic=deterministic)

class DSConvDilatedBlock(nn.Module):
    d_model: int
    kernel_size: int = 7
    dilation: int = 1
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic=True):
        h = nn.LayerNorm()(x)
        h = nn.Conv(
            features=self.d_model,
            kernel_size=(self.kernel_size,),
            feature_group_count=self.d_model, # Depthwise
            padding='SAME',

            name='dw_conv'

        h = nn.gelu(h) # GELU activation
        h = nn.Conv(features=self.d_model, kernel_size=(1,), name='pw_conv')(h)
        h = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(h, deterministic=deterministic)
        return x + h

            # Return zeros with correct shape [batch_size, d_model] after initial dense
            return jnp.zeros((x.shape[0], self.d_model_common), dtype=x.dtype)

        # Initial Dense layer to project input to d_model_common
        x = nn.Dense(self.d_model_common, name="initial_dense")(x)
        x = nn.gelu(x)
        x = nn.Dropout(rate=self.dropout_rate)(x, deterministic=deterministic)

        # Stacked DSConv Dilated Blocks
        for i in range(self.ds_num_blocks):
            dilation = self.ds_dilations[i] if i < len(self.ds_dilations) else self.ds_dilations[-1]
            x = DSConvDilatedBlock(
                d_model=self.d_model_common,
                kernel_size=self.ds_kernel_size,
                dilation=dilation,
                dropout_rate=self.dropout_rate,
                name=f"dsconv_block_{i}"

class HybridPooling(nn.Module):
    dropout_rate: float = 0.1

        if h.shape[1] == 0:
            # Return zeros with correct shape [batch_size, 2*d_model]
            return jnp.zeros((h.shape[0], 2 * h.shape[2]), dtype=h.dtype) # h.shape[2] is d_model_common

        mean_pooled = jnp.mean(h, axis=1)
        max_pooled = jnp.max(h, axis=1)
        x_pooled = jnp.concatenate([mean_pooled, max_pooled], axis=-1)
